STATUS: fail
SUMMARY: The flag-on hiding, cleanup, refcount, slot, root and live-announcer probes all held. One shadow-specific gap reproduces: content added to an outer call's shadow root while a nested call is active is never hidden, even after the nested call is cleaned up. The existing `shouldUseInert` test never reaches the inert branch because jsdom has no `inert`.
FILES TOUCHED: none (probe files `zzProbe.test.js`, `zzProbeInert.test.js`, `zzProbeInertSetup.js`, `zzProbeDuring.test.js` were created in `packages/@react-aria/overlays/test/` and deleted; `git status` matches the start: the same three modified files)
FINDINGS:
- [blocking] Criterion 2/4 fail for nested calls. The outer call's target is in shadow root A. A nested call is then made with a light-DOM target, and a new `<input>` is appended to A while the nested call is active. After the nested cleanup the input is still not hidden. Outer's observer is disconnected while the nested call is alive, and the nested call does not observe A. Probe: `expect(during).toHaveAttribute('aria-hidden','true')` → received `null`. The probe for the light-DOM equivalent fails the same way, so this is a pre-existing gap in the nesting design that the diff extends to shadow roots. The orchestrator should decide whether it is in scope.
- [minor] Criterion "works with shouldUseInert: true" is not exercised by the suite. `'inert' in HTMLElement.prototype` is `false` in this jsdom (`SUPPORTS_INERT false`), so `shouldUseInert` silently falls back to aria-hidden. With an inert polyfill loaded before the module, the inert branch passes (I1, I2: shadow siblings and sibling hosts get `inert`, and cleanup restores them). The repo test only proves the aria-hidden fallback.
- [minor] Closed shadow roots (`mode:'closed'`) are never walked, because `element.shadowRoot` is null. Siblings inside them are not hidden. Not in the criteria; not reproduced as a criterion failure (P14 confirmed the host itself is hidden).
- [minor] Style: `root as Element` and `acceptNode(root as Element)` casts on a ShadowRoot, and the per-node loop over `slots` in `acceptNode` is O(nodes × slots).
CHECKS:
- P1 outer cleanup first, targets in two shadow roots → pass (inner still hides B; A additions not hidden; both hosts restored)
- P2 inner cleanup first, outer resumes hiding A additions → pass
- P3 shadow addition during nested lifetime, hidden after inner cleanup → FAIL (`null`, see blocking)
- P3b light-DOM analog of P3 → FAIL (same pre-existing behavior)
- P4 refcount, same shadow sibling held by two calls → pass (kept after inner, removed after outer)
- P5 `keepVisible` element added later to shadow root, plus child → pass
- P6 content added to a hidden sibling host's shadow root not separately hidden → pass
- P7 `root` is an element inside a shadow root → pass (nothing above root hidden)
- P8 `root` light container containing a shadow host; outside host's root not walked → pass
- P9/I1/I2 `shouldUseInert` with polyfilled inert, siblings, additions, sibling host, cleanup → pass
- P12 after cleanup, shadow and light additions untouched → pass (first run was contaminated by a leaked observer from an earlier failing probe; rerun clean)
- P14 closed shadow sibling host → host hidden, pass
- P15 two calls on the same shadow root, inner cleanup keeps outer's siblings and additions hidden → pass
- P16 two-level target with level-1 siblings and a light-DOM sibling → pass
- D1 shadow addition during nested lifetime, observed before cleanup → `null` (same as P3)
OPEN QUESTIONS: Is the nested-call gap (P3) in scope for this change, given the light-DOM path has the same behavior? If yes, it is a blocking fix. The inert coverage gap probably needs a polyfill or a jsdom-capable test.
